edition.en: Text from Chinese Wikisource, transcribed from volume 1 of the Complete Works of Lu Xun (1948 printing); first published in The Short Story Magazine (小說月報) 13:12, December 1922, and collected in Call to Arms (吶喊), 1923.
edition.zh: 据维基文库，录自《鲁迅全集》第一卷（1948 年印本）；初刊于 1922 年 12 月《小说月报》第十三卷第十二号，收入《呐喊》（1923）。

basis.en: First published in 1922; the author died in 1936. Public domain by age: the author died before 1956 and the text was published before 1931.
basis.zh: 1922 年首次发表，作者卒于 1936 年。作者卒于 1956 年前、作品发表于 1931 年前，按年限属公有领域。

note.en: First two dismal evenings at the opera in Beijing, then the real subject: a boy’s summer night on the river, a borrowed boat, a performance the children leave halfway through, and beans stolen and boiled on the way home. It is here because it shows how a remembered night becomes better than any later version of the same thing. Notice the last line, where the beans and the play are joined and neither can be had again.
note.zh: 先写在北京看戏的两回狼狈，然后才是真正要写的：一个孩子的夏夜，借来的航船，看到一半就走的戏，还有归途中偷来煮吃的罗汉豆。收在这里，是因为它写出了一个被记住的夜晚，如何胜过后来同样的东西。留意最后一句，豆和戏连在一起，都再也得不到了。

excerpt.orig: 眞的，一直到現在，我實在再沒有喫到那夜似的好豆，——也不再看到那夜似的好戲了。
excerpt.en: It is true. Right up to now, I have really never again eaten beans as good as those of that night, nor seen another opera as good as the one I saw that night.
excerpt.zh: 真的，一直到现在，我实在再没有吃到那夜似的好豆，——也不再看到那夜似的好戏了。

gloss.en: The first year of the Republic: 1912. Lu Xun came to Beijing that May to work in the Ministry of Education.
gloss.zh: 民国元年：1912 年。这年 5 月，鲁迅到北京教育部任职。

gloss.en: Tan Jiaotian: Tan Xinpei (1847–1917), the most celebrated singer of old-man roles in Peking opera, whose stage name was Xiao Jiaotian.
gloss.zh: 谭叫天：谭鑫培（1847–1917），京剧老生的一代宗师，艺名小叫天。

gloss.en: The First Stage: a large theatre built in Beijing in 1914 on the lines of a Western playhouse.
gloss.zh: 第一舞台：1914 年在北京建成的新式大剧场，仿照西式剧院的格局。

gloss.en: Role types of Chinese opera: laodan, old woman; xiaodan, young woman; huadan, lively young woman; laosheng, older man; xiaosheng, young man.
gloss.zh: 戏曲的行当：老旦演老年妇女，小旦演年轻女子，花旦演活泼的少女，老生演中老年男子，小生演青年男子。

gloss.en: Mulian: a disciple of the Buddha who went down into hell to save his mother. ‘Mulian Rescues His Mother’ was a favourite of temple and village stages.
gloss.zh: 目连：佛陀的弟子，相传曾入地狱救母。“目连救母”是寺庙和乡间舞台上很受欢迎的戏。

gloss.en: The opening of ‘Si Gan’ in the Book of Songs, a poem for the building of a palace: the kind of text a boy had to learn by heart at school.
gloss.zh: 语出《诗经·小雅·斯干》，是一首庆贺宫室落成的诗；这正是私塾里孩子要背诵的书。

gloss.en: 賽: a festival of offerings and processions for a god. 社戲 is opera staged for the god of the land (社) at such a festival.
gloss.zh: 赛：迎神赛会，为酬神而举行的祭祀和游行。社戏是在这类节日里为土地神（社）演的戏。

gloss.en: 航船: the boat that carried passengers and goods between a village and the town on a regular run, out in the morning and back at night.
gloss.zh: 航船：定期往来于乡村与城镇之间、载客运货的船，早出晚归。

gloss.en: Black-awning boats: the small boats of Shaoxing, roofed with arched mats of bamboo painted black. The passenger boat’s awning was white.
gloss.zh: 乌篷船：绍兴一带的小船，船篷用竹篾编成，涂成黑色。航船的篷是白的。

gloss.en: 羅漢豆: the Shaoxing name for broad beans (蠶豆).
gloss.zh: 罗汉豆：绍兴一带对蚕豆的叫法。

gloss.en: The night was divided into five watches of about two hours each; the third watch runs from about eleven to one.
gloss.zh: 三更：旧时把一夜分为五更，每更约两小时，三更约在夜里十一点到一点。

gloss.en: 姑奶奶: what the people of her old home call a daughter who has married away; here, the narrator’s mother.
gloss.zh: 姑奶奶：娘家人对已出嫁女儿的称呼，这里指“我”的母亲。
